column11: an analogue, because giredestrant is not approved and has no price of its own. Orserdu (elacestrant) is the only approved oral selective estrogen receptor degrader and its label is the same population the giredestrant application is filed in - ESR1-mutated, ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer after at least one line of endocrine therapy. CMS Medicare Part D Spending by Drug 2024 (data.cms.gov dataset 7e0b4365-fd63-4a29-8f5e-e0ac9f66a81b, Brnd_Name Orserdu, Mftr_Name Overall): $258,846,197.93 over 2,633 beneficiaries = $98,308 per beneficiary a year, on 414,970 dosage units at a weighted $703.99 each
column12: the comparator is chosen rather than measured, and that is the weak part. The case for a higher figure: giredestrant would launch with a positive randomised Phase 3 behind it where Orserdu launched on EMERALD, and Roche has priced into stronger data before. The case for lower: by the time giredestrant is selling, elacestrant, camizestrant and imlunestrant are all competing for the same prescription. No Genentech WAC exists to check this against, because the product is not on sale

column11: a Part D anchor, so the CMS figure above is gross of manufacturer rebates and a real deduction applies. The house figure for a branded oral oncolytic is the one lly_verzenio carries, 18% off list. MedPAC's own reading of the class is consistent with a deduction of that order rather than a larger one: in its June 2023 Report to the Congress, Chapter 2, rebates for antineoplastics 'grew more than 800 percent' over the window while the effect on net cost stayed small because gross brand spending grew as fast
column12: a judgement. Oral oncology rebates shallowly because a payer has little ability to switch a patient off a targeted agent, but the oral SERD class will be crowded by launch, which is the case for a larger deduction. Roche publishes no US gross-to-net reconciliation, so there is no company figure to replace this with

column11: from the registrational study's own median progression-free survival. evERA (NCT05306340), 373 patients randomised, 207 of them with ESR1-mutated tumours: median progression-free survival 10.0 months with giredestrant plus everolimus against 5.5 months with standard endocrine therapy plus everolimus, hazard ratio 0.38 (95% CI 0.27-0.54, p<0.001) (Mayer EL, Tolaney SM, Martin M, et al., 'Giredestrant plus Everolimus in Advanced Breast Cancer', N Engl J Med 2026;395(13):1285-1298, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2602457, PMID 42814929). At a constant hazard, 1 - exp(-ln2 / (10/12)) = 0.5647
column12: the ESR1-mutated median was taken rather than the 8.8 months of the intention-to-treat population, because the application under review is in ESR1-mutated disease; the intention-to-treat figure would give 0.611, a faster turnover. Progression-free survival overstates time on drug where treatment stops early for toxicity and understates it where it continues past progression

column1: ROG
column11: the ESR1-mutated share, which is the population the application under review covers. Roche's own statement of the real-world frequency: 'Up to 40% of patients in the post-CDK inhibitor setting carry ESR1 mutations' (Roche media release med-cor-2026-10-01, 2026-10-01, reporting the evERA publication). The published circulating-tumour-DNA literature puts the share at about 30% of ER-positive HER2-negative metastatic patients overall and about 40% at progression after first-line aromatase inhibitor plus CDK4/6 inhibitor
column12: two things to argue with. First, evERA's own enrolled population was 55.5% ESR1-mutated (207 of 373; N Engl J Med 2026;395(13):1285-1298), well above the figure taken here, which is the case for a larger layer; a trial that tests circulating tumour DNA in every screened patient will find more mutations than routine practice does, which is why the real-world figure was taken instead. Second, and biasing this high, no further narrowing for line of therapy is applied: the 160,000 is the whole prevalent metastatic HR-positive HER2-negative stock, while the eligible patient has already progressed on a CDK4/6 inhibitor. At steady state nearly all of this pool passes through that point, but not all of it is there at once

column1: ROG
column11: a judgement. The case for a high share: this would be the first oral SERD with a randomised Phase 3 showing a progression-free survival benefit in combination rather than as monotherapy, the hazard ratio in the ESR1-mutated population is 0.38, and the comparator it displaces is exemestane or fulvestrant with everolimus, which is poorly tolerated. The case against, and why the number is not higher: Orserdu is already approved in exactly this population and held 2,633 Medicare Part D beneficiaries in 2024, camizestrant and imlunestrant are arriving on their own Phase 3 data, and Roche's own persevERA study failed to beat letrozole in the first line, so the molecule has no claim on the setting ahead of this one
column12: a peak share is settled by years of sales rather than by an event, so no replacement is named

column11: filed, with a dated decision. The FDA accepted the giredestrant new drug application in ESR1-mutated ER-positive advanced breast cancer on the evERA data and set a goal date of 2026-12-18, with a second application in early-stage disease on lidERA at 2026-11-30 (Roche media releases med-cor-2026-10-01 and med-cor-2026-06-02). evERA met its primary endpoint in both the intention-to-treat and ESR1-mutated populations and is published (N Engl J Med 2026;395(13):1285-1298). The remaining transition is NDA/BLA to approval on the Oncology cut: 0.920 (n=324) (BIO/Informa Pharma Intelligence/QLS Advisors, Clinical Development Success Rates 2011-2020, Figure 2 page 7; data/pos_transitions.csv)
